headline: With n slots, the answer lies in 1 through n+1
statement: Find the smallest positive integer absent from nums, in linear time and constant auxiliary space. You may rearrange nums.
intuition: For n input positions, the smallest missing positive number must be between 1 and n + 1. Use the array itself to remember which of these numbers exist. Place value 1 at index 0, value 2 at index 1, and so on. Then look for the first position with the wrong value.
approach: For each index, repeatedly swap its value into its home if it is between 1 and n.
Stop when the current value is out of range or its home already contains that value.
Scan left to right for the first slot not containing index+1; otherwise return n+1.
correctness: Every swap permanently fills a previously incorrect home with its matching value. No correct home is displaced, so at most n such swaps occur. At the end every present value in 1..n occupies its home; the first missing home identifies the smallest absent positive.
bruteForce: Try 1, 2, 3, ... and scan nums for each candidate: O(n²) time. A set gives O(n) time but uses O(n) space.

complexity.explanation: Time O(n); additional space O(1). Output storage is excluded unless stated.

pitfalls: Ignore zero, negatives, and values larger than n.
Check for duplicate values before swapping to avoid an infinite loop.
